sources.note: Nothing. Says 'Malasar is an unclassified southern language.. converse with each other in a patois debased form of Tamil'; announces a grammar, a Malasar-English-Tamil e-dictionary and an ethnolinguistic profile as outcomes of a documentation project 'in progress' (pilot survey and fieldwork done). SPPEL grammatical-sketches, dictionaries, vocabularies, ethnolinguistic-sketches and publications pages checked: no Malasar item published (only 'A Sketch Grammar of Eravalla' 2023 and a 'Malayan-Malayalam-English Dictionary' 2022 for the Thrissur Malayan, a different community).

sources.citation: Varghese, Bijumon (comp.). 2015. The Tribes of Palakkad, Kerala: A Sociolinguistic Profile. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-028. Dallas: SIL International. 173 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (lexical similarity, RTT, SRT, LUAV). Sec. 1.3 (p.2) and 2.4 'Malasar' (pp.9-10) say only that Malasar 'speak a form of Tamil' (p.13) / Nattu Malasar 'a dialect of Malayalam with a lot of Tamil admixture', Kong Malasar 'Tamil as their mother tongue' (p.10, after Menon 1996:247). Two Malasar 210-item IPA wordlists (Appendix B3: 'Malasar, Oriental Estate' and 'Malasar pasha, Ellakkadu') carry no stress marks; p.47 says the data 'have not undergone thorough phonological and grammatical analysis'. a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|supraseg|prosod|intonati…

sources.note: Eravallan (erav1242) is Malasar's closest relative (77-86% lexical similarity per ISO CR 2006-006); this CIIL sketch would show the Tamiloid-tribal stress pattern and may mention Malasar comparatively. Not a Malasar statement, but the nearest published phonology. Print purchase only (Rs., CIIL store).
